claims.text: JPMorgan paid USVI $75m (Sept 2023): $30m charities, $25m anti-trafficking law enforcement, $20m legal fees; no admission; USVI had sought at least $190m incl. a $150m civil penalty; alleged JPM kept him as a 'valued client' after 2006 arrest and 2008 plea; JPM 'deeply regrets any association'; Staley settled with JPM confidentially.
Estate paid USVI more than $105m (Dec 2022) plus half the proceeds of selling both islands; executors deny wrongdoing.

sources.label: Al Jazeera, 'JPMorgan to pay US Virgin Islands $75m to settle Epstein lawsuit', 26 Sept 2023
Fox Business / AP, 'Epstein estate reaches $105M settlement with US Virgin Islands', 1 Dec 2022

claims.text: NYDFS consent order, $150m (July 2020): Deutsche Bank onboarded Epstein 2013; failed to monitor despite public criminal record; hundreds of transactions totalling millions; payments to Russian models, women's tuition, hotel and rent, women with Eastern European surnames, alleged co-conspirators; over $7m settlements and over $6m to law firms; more than $800,000 suspicious cash withdrawals over about four years; Sewing: onboarding 'a critical mistake'.
JPMorgan filed suspicious activity reports on over $1bn of Epstein-linked transactions weeks after his death in 2019 (NYT).

UK tribunal (26 June 2025) upheld the FCA's 2023 ban on Jes Staley; fine cut from £1.8m to about £1.1m; FCA found Barclays' 2019 letter misleading and Staley reckless; contact via his daughter until at least Feb 2017; Barclays withheld £17.8m in awards.

sources.label: CNBC, 'Deutsche Bank fined $150 million penalty for relationship with Jeffrey Epstein', 7 July 2020
Seeking Alpha, citing the New York Times: JPMorgan reported over $1 billion in suspicious Epstein transactions weeks after his death
AP/PTI, 'Ex-Barclays boss Staley loses bid to overturn UK ban over Epstein ties', 26 June 2025

claims.text: Epstein said he invested clients' fortunes in currency markets (Vanity Fair, per BI).

Claimed solo investing with ~150 back-office staff (New York mag figure) vs ~20 in a 2002 court filing; claimed to work only with billionaires; hedge-fund managers sceptical: 'It's hard to make a billion dollars quietly'; one guessed index fund or Treasuries.
